findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The directive matcher ignores negation and 'already filed' wording, so some plain exclusions would still queue a request.
findings.evidence: Rule (b) matches 'propose' within three words of request(s)/job(s), so 'Do not propose new jobs for the backlog' queues a request. Rule (a) matches 'as a separate request', so 'Planner deadline survival is already filed as a separate request (introspection ...)' queues a duplicate of work that is already filed. Decision 2 dropped the id-based skip, so nothing catches this case. The brief's own pj25 item escapes only because its wording happens to lack 'as'. Fix: Reject a match when 'not', 'no', 'never', "don't" or 'already' comes within three words before the matched phrase, or when the clause holds 'filed', 'queued' or 'tracked'. Add these negative cases to the table in `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_pure`.
findings.location: Decision 4 (`is_follow_up` rules (a) and (b)); followups.rs table test

findings.summary: The plan does not say which job-ending paths with a reading never reach `close_dispatched`.
findings.evidence: The reading says 'when a job ends with a reading'. A job declined or refused at reading, or stopped before dispatch (for example `replay_holds_over_threshold_rejects_the_job_and_records_the_list`, run/tests.rs:2118), has a reading but never reaches close.rs:38. The plan lists only the hold and retry_landing paths. Fix: Add a dependents entry stating that jobs ended before dispatch (declined, refused, replay-rejected, preflight-stopped) queue nothing, and why. Optionally pin this with an assertion in the criterion 2 close test.
findings.location: Dependents: 'which closes reach the new line'

findings.summary: The criterion 1 table cites 'this brief's six real out_of_scope items', but the brief lists five.
findings.evidence: The brief's Out of scope section has five bullets: planner deadline, backfill, hestia findings, refusal rules/prompts/config, and reprioritizing. Fix: Say five, or name the sixth item, for example by splitting the athena.toml/defaults.toml list out on its own.

findings.summary: The ui lines printed before the commit can report requests that were never committed.
findings.evidence: `follow_up_files` runs and prints before `land_or_block` or `commit_records_with`. If the gate refuses the closing commit or landing bails (close.rs:416-418), the ui has already said the requests were queued. Fix: Word the lines as 'will queue', or print them after the closing commit succeeds, using the returned `Finished`.
findings.location: Step 4 (`follow_up_files` prints one ui line per queued item)

summary: I checked the plan's main claims against the code, and they hold. `close_dispatched` (run/close.rs:8-168) is where a job that ran is closed. `push_closing_records` is at line 38, and the plain commit's closure clones `closing.files` on each attempt (close.rs:132-146). `retried_job` is public and re-exported (reading/retry.rs:201, reading.rs:62/70). `RequestQueue::apply` → `StewardRequest::from_change` → `StewardRequest::new` (steward.rs:535-683) builds and writes the request on REQUEST_CHANNEL. `from_change` takes Files from the whole text, falling back to `records/` when the source is a job reference, so the plan is right to guard each line. In the gate, `closing_jobs` (invariant.rs:240-269) counts only candidate/verification/outcome files, so a closing commit that also adds request.json for other jobs does not trigger SeveralJobs. `landing` checks only the Athena-Job trailer against the landed job. I grepped every test fixture's `out_of_scope` (run/tests.rs, run_pin_tests.rs, work_decisions.rs, scope_guard.rs, reading.rs, athena-agent fake.rs:270-291, athena-cli common/mod.rs and retry.rs). None of them matches the directive rule, so no existing test starts queuing requests. The plan includes the commit-shape table and a realistic-branch fixture with ask, intervention and landing commits, and no classification function changes. Each demonstration names a real seam (`athena_with`, `finished_job`, `FAILS_ON_EDIT`, `low_once_verifying`, `rated_scenario`, `queued_ids`, `improvement_of`) and would fail without the behavior. The close.rs edit outside the listed deliverables is justified by the code, and Athena has already flagged it. My remaining findings are minor: the wording rule ignores negation and "already filed as a separate request" wording, and the plan does not say which job-ending paths with a reading never reach `close_dispatched`.
